qualitative.note: Fails Gate 1 (Reject Standard (a) and (b)). Coinbase operates a crypto-native brokerage and exchange model lacking a multi-cycle public operating track record (direct listed in 2021). Its economic engine is tied to speculative crypto bull/bear cycles, driving extreme boom-bust volatility ($3.62B net income in FY21, -$2.62B net loss in FY22, $95M in FY23, $2.58B in FY24, and ~$1.26B in FY25). Furthermore, its balance sheet carries direct crypto treasuries and opaque counterparty/protocol risks, and a growing share of revenue (~45-50% in FY24-FY25 via subscription & services) is dependent on USDC reserve interest sharing with Circle, introducing heavy macro interest rate sensitivity. Outside circle of competence and fails external verifiability under the Munger standard.
qualitative.evidence: Founded in 2012 and direct-listed in April 2021, Coinbase is the leading US-based cryptocurrency exchange, operating transaction trading, custody, and subscription & services (primarily USDC stablecoin interest sharing with Circle, staking rewards, and Base Layer-2 network). Financial history demonstrates severe non-economic cycle volatility: FY21 revenue was $7.84B with $3.62B net income; FY22 collapsed to $3.19B revenue and a -$2.62B net loss; FY23 was $3.11B revenue and $95M net income; FY24 rebounded to $6.56B revenue and $2.58B net income; FY25 revenue reached $7.18B with ~$1.26B net income. Transaction fees represent high retail take-rates subject to secular compression against institutional brokers (Robinhood, Fidelity, Charles Schwab) and spot ETF wrappers. While the SEC civil enforcement action was voluntarily dismissed in February 2025 under changed regulatory leadership, the underlying business remains inherently speculative, capital returns are unproven across standard macro cycles, and balance sheet exposure to crypto treasuries and off-balance sheet stablecoin reserve mechanics violates Gate 1 external verifiability.
